successCriteria.description: The `ILeaveRequestService` interface is defined in `src/modules/leave-request/leave-request.service.interface.ts` and exposes exactly 8 methods: `createDraft(dto: CreateLeaveRequestDto): Promise<LeaveRequest>`, `submit(id: string): Promise<LeaveRequest>`, `approve(id: string, approverId: string): Promise<LeaveRequest>`, `reject(id: string, approverId: string): Promise<LeaveRequest>`, `cancel(id: string): Promise<LeaveRequest>`, `findById(id: string): Promise<LeaveRequest | null>`, `findByEmployeeId(employeeId: string): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>`, `query(params: LeaveRequestQueryParams): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>`.

`createDraft` validates that the employee exists (via `IEmployeeRepository.findById`), the policy exists and `isActive` is true (via `ILeavePolicyRepository.findById`), and `startDate <= endDate`; it then creates a `LeaveRequest` with `status = DRAFT` via `ILeaveRequestRepository.create` and returns it.

`submit` validates the request is in `DRAFT` status, checks `minimumNoticeDays` from the associated policy (if set, `startDate` must be >= `now + minimumNoticeDays` calendar days), computes `daysRequested` using the BINDING formula `(endDate.getTime() - startDate.getTime()) / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24) + 1`, looks up the balance via `ILeaveBalanceRepository.findByEmployeeAndPolicy` for the fiscal year `startDate.getFullYear()`, verifies `remainingDays >= daysRequested`, and transitions the request to `SUBMITTED`.

`approve` validates the request is `SUBMITTED`, validates `approverId === employee.managerId` (obtained via `IEmployeeRepository.findById`), deducts `daysRequested` from `LeaveBalance.usedDays` and recalculates `remainingDays = totalEntitlement - usedDays`, sets `status = APPROVED`, `approvedBy = approverId`, `approvedAt = now`.
`reject` validates the request is `SUBMITTED`, validates `approverId === employee.managerId`, sets `status = REJECTED` without modifying any balance.

`cancel` validates the request is `APPROVED` or `SUBMITTED`; if `APPROVED`, restores `usedDays` on the balance by subtracting `daysRequested` and recalculating `remainingDays`; sets `status = CANCELLED`, `cancelledAt = now`.
`findById`, `findByEmployeeId`, and `query` delegate directly to the corresponding `ILeaveRequestRepository` methods and return their results unchanged.

Every state-changing method (`createDraft`, `submit`, `approve`, `reject`, `cancel`) throws a typed error (with `{ error: string; code: string }` shape) when its preconditions are violated — not-found (404 semantics), validation (400 semantics), or business-rule conflict (409 semantics) — and no partial state mutation persists on failure.

Jest unit tests in `tests/unit/modules/leave-request/leave-request.service.test.ts` cover all valid state transitions (DRAFT→SUBMITTED→APPROVED, DRAFT→SUBMITTED→REJECTED, SUBMITTED→CANCELLED, APPROVED→CANCELLED), all error paths (missing employee, inactive policy, invalid dates, insufficient notice, insufficient balance, wrong approver, invalid state transitions), and the BINDING day-counting formula with at least 3 distinct date ranges.

constraints: The BINDING day-counting formula `daysRequested = (endDate.getTime() - startDate.getTime()) / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24) + 1` must be used at every call site that computes leave duration — submit balance check, approve deduction, cancel restoration. No alternative formula, no weekend/holiday exclusion, no time-of-day adjustment.

Fiscal year is determined as `startDate.getFullYear()` (calendar year Jan 1 – Dec 31). The balance lookup in `submit`, `approve`, and `cancel` must use this fiscal year when calling `ILeaveBalanceRepository.findByEmployeeAndPolicy`.

All dates are full-day granularity — no half-days, no hours, no time-of-day considerations. `startDate` and `endDate` are treated as date-only values. The `daysRequested` result is always a positive integer.
outOfScope: HTTP routes, controllers, and Fastify plugin registration — these belong to Phase 9.

Notification creation on lifecycle transitions (notify manager on submit, notify employee on approve/reject/cancel) — the `INotificationService` is not a constructor dependency in this phase; notification integration is deferred to Phase 10.

Audit log creation for state-changing operations — `IAuditLogRepository` is not a constructor dependency of `LeaveRequestService` in this phase. Audit integration is deferred to a later phase or handled by a separate cross-cutting mechanism.

entityInvariants.invariant: Lifecycle state machine: DRAFT → SUBMITTED → (APPROVED | REJECTED). From SUBMITTED or APPROVED, may transition to CANCELLED. No other transitions are valid. The service must reject any attempt to transition outside this graph (e.g., DRAFT→APPROVED, REJECTED→CANCELLED, APPROVED→SUBMITTED).

When `status === APPROVED`, both `approvedBy` and `approvedAt` must be non-null. When `status !== APPROVED`, both must be null. `cancelledAt` must be null unless `status === CANCELLED`, in which case it must be non-null.

`remainingDays` MUST equal `totalEntitlement - usedDays` at all times. Every mutation to `usedDays` (deduction on approve, restoration on cancel) MUST recalculate `remainingDays` accordingly before persisting.
A balance with `status === 'CLOSED'` must not be mutated. The service must check the balance status before deducting or restoring `usedDays` and reject the operation if the balance is CLOSED.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Caller identity is not validated by the service itself (RBAC is enforced at the controller/route layer in Phase 9). The service accepts the `employeeId` from the DTO and trusts the caller.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws if employee not found, policy not found or inactive, or startDate > endDate. Error shape: `{ error: string; code: string }`.

Throws if request not found, request not in DRAFT status, minimumNoticeDays violated, balance not found, insufficient remainingDays, or balance is CLOSED. Error shape: `{ error: string; code: string }`.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: RBAC deferred to controller layer (Phase 9). The service validates that `approverId === employee.managerId` as a business rule, not as an auth concern.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws if request not found, request not in SUBMITTED status, approverId does not match employee.managerId, balance not found, or balance is CLOSED. Error shape: `{ error: string; code: string }`.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: RBAC deferred to controller layer (Phase 9). The service validates that `approverId === employee.managerId` as a business rule.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws if request not found, request not in SUBMITTED status, or approverId does not match employee.managerId. Error shape: `{ error: string; code: string }`.
Throws if request not found, request not in SUBMITTED or APPROVED status, or (if APPROVED) balance not found or balance is CLOSED. Error shape: `{ error: string; code: string }`.
Read-only; no business-rule errors. Return null or empty array on no results.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The `LeaveRequest` entity returned by all service methods must conform to the `LeaveRequest` interface defined in `src/modules/leave-request/leave-request.model.ts` — same fields, same types, same nullability.

The `LeaveRequestQueryParams` parameter of `query` must match the interface defined in `src/shared/types/index.ts` — fields `employeeId`, `status`, `leavePolicyId`, `startDateFrom`, `startDateTo` with the same types and optionality.

The `CreateLeaveRequestDto` parameter of `createDraft` must match the interface defined in `src/shared/types/index.ts` — fields `employeeId`, `leavePolicyId`, `startDate`, `endDate`, `reason` with the same types and optionality.

The `LeaveBalance.remainingDays` invariant (`remainingDays = totalEntitlement - usedDays`) defined in `src/modules/leave-balance/leave-balance.model.ts` must be preserved by every balance mutation in `approve` and `cancel`.

The `LeaveRequest` lifecycle invariant documented in `src/modules/leave-request/leave-request.model.ts` (DRAFT → SUBMITTED → APPROVED | REJECTED; cancellable from SUBMITTED or APPROVED) must be enforced by every state-transitioning method.

integrationPoints.why: Service calls `findById`, `create`, and `update` on this repository for all leave request persistence operations.
Service calls `findById` on this repository during `createDraft` (to validate policy exists and isActive) and during `submit` (to read `minimumNoticeDays`).
Service calls `findById` on this repository during `createDraft` (to validate employee exists) and during `approve`/`reject` (to retrieve `managerId` for approver validation).
